title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Ateliers' notes (ch. IX/IX bis). These belong to Grothendieck's attempt, in the spirit of the 'géométrie modérée' (tame topology) programme of the Esquisse, to axiomatise 'figures', their 'supports' and their subdivisions inside an ambient universe Σ = Σ_A. Some form of constructibility condition plays the role of the tame category of spaces. On the previous page he planned to test whether supports are as crucial as he suspected. He also began a 'philosophical critique': defining material operations (consumption, production) forces one to compose strata that are not compatible or commensurable.

This page states the problem explicitly.
(1) Until now he has only considered supports, and operations on supports, in the constructible case ('ens. constr.', plus some supplementary class, written 'supp. ℒ ...'), together with suitable families of such supports.
(2) He now sees an 'internal contradiction'. Even his latest presentation of a figure, written X|Y (a decomposition into two strata X, Y, required only to be in some sense 'ind. disj.', presumably independent or disjoint), forces him to consider strata that need not be constructible, nor even 'commensurable'. That is, they need not admit common refinements or comparisons with other subdivisions.
(3) Yet he finds it indispensable to have an intrinsic description of the supports underlying a figure, as objects of a universe (here Σ_A) that is independent of the given figure.
(4) The sentence runs on to the next page ('…mon flair m'aurait-il trompé, pour une fois ?'). There he proposes either to watch every appeal to supports carefully, or to restrict to the subcategory Σ_cons of constructible supports, with totally versus partially defined operations.

In modern terms, this is the familiar foundational tension in tame topology. One wants a class of 'definable/constructible' sets that is stable under all the operations one needs (boolean operations, images, strata of decompositions). Then supports can be intrinsic objects of a fixed ambient category, and any two subdivisions have a common refinement. If the class is not closed under the operations, the formalism breaks. o-minimal structures (and semialgebraic/subanalytic geometry) resolve exactly this by fixing a structure in which all strata produced are definable and any two definable cell decompositions/triangulations admit a common refinement.
errors: No mathematical error. The page is a self-diagnosis of a foundational inconsistency, not a claim. The contradiction is stated only informally; which notion of 'constructible' and 'commensurable' is meant depends on earlier chapters not shown.

ideas.what: Supports of figures should be intrinsic objects of an ambient universe Σ_A, independent of the figure; a class of constructible supports is needed that is stable under the strata arising in presentations X|Y.
ideas.modern_name: closure axioms of an o-minimal structure / tame topology; definable sets as intrinsic supports
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (o-minimality, 1984–86); Shiota, Hironaka, Łojasiewicz (semialgebraic/subanalytic)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on 'topologie modérée' (programmatic only)

ideas.what: Commensurability of subdivisions/strata (existence of common refinements) as a necessary condition for operations on supports.
ideas.modern_name: common refinement of definable cell decompositions / triangulations; Hauptvermutung-type issues
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology; o-minimal triangulation theorem (van den Dries)

deep.surprise_reason: A methodological diary entry noticing that the 'Ateliers' formalism quietly uses non-constructible, non-commensurable strata. It is the standard foundational issue that o-minimality addresses. It is of biographical and historical interest but contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 7: 'Il y a [-dans-] là' – the struck word is likely 'dans' or similar; reading OK.
'(dans [?] = quelles notions[?] "ind. disj.")' is more plausibly '(sauf qu'elles soient "ind. disj.")' or similar.

'comme un objet de ma[?] figure (en l'occurrence Σd)' should read roughly 'comme un objet d'un univers (en l'occurrence Σ_A) indépendant de ladite figure'. The underlined 'indépen-/dant' is split across lines.
Final words 'On veut plus[?]' are likely 'Ou mon flair', which continues on p.120 as 'm'aurait-il trompé, pour une fois ?'
